start.speaker: narrator
start.text: The road ends at a gate that hasn't closed properly in years. Beyond it, dry grass runs to the horizon.

n1.speaker: tendai
n1.text: So. You're the founder's grandchild. Mind the gate—it's been rotten for years.

choices.text: You must be Tendai. Gran wrote about you.

n3a.speaker: tendai
n3a.text: Did she now. Hopefully not the story about the honey badger and my lunch.

n3b.speaker: tendai
n3b.text: Quiet is what's left when the animals give up on a place.

n4.speaker: tendai
n4.text: Thirty-one years I've worked this land. The last eight, mostly on my own.

n5.speaker: tendai
n5.text: Your grandmother kept this reserve alive with her own two hands. When she got sick, it started to slip.

n6.speaker: tendai
n6.text: The fences are broken, the waterholes are dry, and what animals we have left are thirsty.

n7.speaker: tendai
n7.text: Do you want to see the waterhole first, or the fences?

water.speaker: tendai
water.text: Waterhole A. Half the plains used to drink here. Now look at it—cracked mud.

w2.speaker: tendai
w2.text: The old pump died years ago, so for now we do it the hard way. Click the waterhole to pour in water, or hold the button and keep pumping.

w3.speaker: tendai
w3.text: It loses water every day, twice as fast in the dry season. Hover over it and it tells you exactly how much, and why.

w4.speaker: tendai
w4.text: Get it to 30 or more and keep it there for three days. The animals will remember the way.

w5.speaker: tendai
w5.text: The gate can wait a little. Only a little.

fence.speaker: tendai
fence.text: The main gate. Trucks, tourists, poachers—everything comes through here. Right now it's a gate in name only.

f2.speaker: tendai
f2.text: Click the broken stretch of fence by the gate to mend it. Twenty for wire and posts, and a day's work.

f3.speaker: tendai
f3.text: Dashed lines on the map are broken fences. Solid lines are sound. Remember that.

f4.speaker: tendai
f4.text: After the gate, water. Without water nothing else out here matters.

start.speaker: tendai
start.text: Look at that—real water. Keep it topped up and the herds will notice.

g2.speaker: tendai
g2.text: Now the gate. Click the broken fence by the gate to mend it. Twenty for wire and posts, and a day's work.

g3.speaker: tendai
g3.text: Dashed lines on the map are broken fences. Solid lines are sound.

start.speaker: tendai
start.text: Listen to that. It closes. First thing that's worked properly here in years.

b_end.speaker: tendai
b_end.text: A shut gate keeps the village cattle out and honest people honest. The dishonest ones we'll deal with later.

wt1.speaker: tendai
wt1.text: Now, water. Waterhole A is the heart of the plains, and it's bone dry.

wt2.speaker: tendai
wt2.text: Click the waterhole to pour water in, or hold the button to keep pumping. It's free—just your arms.

wt3.speaker: tendai
wt3.text: It drains every day, faster in the dry season. Hover over it and it'll tell you why.

wt4.speaker: tendai
wt4.text: Get it to 30 or more and keep it there three days running.

start.speaker: tendai
start.text: {player}, the waterhole won't fill itself. Not yet, anyway.

h2.speaker: tendai
h2.text: Click it, or hold the button down. Every click is a bucket.

h3.speaker: tendai
h3.text: Thirty is the mark. Below that the animals won't trust it.

start.speaker: tendai
start.text: Cattle from the village wandered in through the gate again last night.

h2.speaker: tendai
h2.text: Click the broken fence at the gate. Twenty to mend it. Please.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Dust lifts on the far side of the plains. A line of impala picks its way toward the water, ears turning, ready to run.

n2.speaker: tendai
n2.text: There. See the one in front? She's been watching us for days, waiting to see if we meant it.

choices.text: Only a handful. Is that all that's left?

c1.speaker: tendai
c1.text: They always come back to water. It's people they're not sure about.

c2.speaker: tendai
c2.text: Out here, mostly. Some went over the fence into the village fields. Some went into cooking pots.

c3.speaker: tendai
c3.text: Click any herd to see how many there are and what's helping or hurting them. Click open ground to see how a zone is doing.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: That evening Tendai builds a fire beside the old ranger post. The night birds start up one by one.

t2.speaker: tendai
t2.text: You want to know why it all fell apart. Everyone who comes here wants to know.

choices.text: Only if you want to tell me.

t4.speaker: tendai
t4.text: Eight years ago the borehole pump stopped. Just stopped. Your grandmother had it looked at twice. Nobody could find the fault.

t5.speaker: tendai
t5.text: Then came the long drought. The river shrank to puddles. Without the pump, Waterhole A went dry, and the plains herds went with it.

t6.speaker: tendai
t6.text: No water, no animals. No animals, no visitors. No visitors, no wages. One by one the rangers left.

t7.speaker: tendai
t7.text: Then the snares started. Poachers can smell a reserve with nobody watching it.

t8.speaker: tendai
t8.text: Ruth refused to sell. Men in good shoes came every year with offers. She sent every one of them back down the road.

t10.speaker: tendai
t10.text: Somebody had to keep the gate. And I made her a promise.

t11.speaker: tendai
t11.text: Developers. Hotel people. One of them kept coming back. Smiled a lot. I didn't like his smile.

t12.speaker: tendai
t12.text: Anyway. That's the story. The rest of it, we write ourselves.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Three days of water. A gate that shuts. Fresh tracks in the mud at dawn.

c2.speaker: tendai
c2.text: Not bad for a beginner, {player}. Not bad at all.

c3.speaker: tendai
c3.text: But I keep thinking about that pump. Machines wear out slowly. That one died overnight.

c4.speaker: tendai
c4.text: Tomorrow we go and look at it properly. Bring your eyes, not just your hands.

start.speaker: tendai
start.text: Feel that wind? Dry season. Thirty days of it, then the rains.

s2.speaker: tendai
s2.text: In the dry, waterholes drop twice as fast and the grass barely grows. In the wet, the rain does half your work.

s3.speaker: tendai
s3.text: The little sun or raindrop at the top tells you which. Hover over the date and it tells you more.

s5.speaker: tendai
s5.text: They follow the water and the grass. Give them both and they'll stay. Take either away and they go looking.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Late afternoon. Four tawny shapes lie flat in the long grass on the eastern plains.

l2.speaker: tendai
l2.text: The old pride. Four left, out of eleven when your grandmother was young.

l3.speaker: tendai
l3.text: Lions need prey, and prey needs grass and water. Look after the bottom of that ladder and the top looks after itself.

choices.text: Are they a danger to the impala?

l5.speaker: tendai
l5.text: If they drop below four, they won't breed. Watch them—the herd panel will warn you.

l6.speaker: tendai
l6.text: They'll take a few. That's their job. A plains with no lions is just a big farm.
